chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from one who informed him, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

Isma'il ibn Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام was with him, so he said: “O my son, read the mushaf.” He said: “Indeed, I am not in a state of wudu (ablution).” So he said: “Do not touch the writing, and touch the paper.”

key_terms.الْكِتَابَةَ: the written script or text of the Qur'an
key_terms.الْمُصْحَفَ: the written copy of the Qur'an
key_terms.الْوَرَقَ: the paper or material of the pages
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: ritual ablution required for purity in certain acts

ai.seo_question: Can a person without wudu (ablution) touch the mushaf or its pages?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates a legal distinction between touching the written script of the mushaf and touching its paper while not in a state of wudu (ablution). It is used in jurisprudential discussion on ritual purity and the etiquette of handling the Qur'an.
